limit.description: Number of channels to return (max 50). For geo-local or language-specific discovery, request 20+ — relevant local channels may rank below globally popular ones.

sort.description: Result ordering: 'relevance' (default for text searches; ranks by semantic + lexical score), 'subscriberCount' (subscribers desc), 'subsGrowth30d' (30-day subscriber growth desc), 'viewsGrowth30d' (30-day view growth desc), or 'lastVideoPublished' (most recently active first). Pure-filter searches default to subscriberCount desc. Use 'relevance' for ALL topical queries including 'popular/famous/top channels in X' — relevance ranking already favors notable channels. Use field sorts only for explicit metric scans ('most subscribed regardless of topic fit', 'fastest growing'); pair growth sorts with subscriberCountMin (e.g. 1000) because growth percentages explode at tiny subscriber bases.

tools.name: vidiq_comment_insights
tools.title: YouTube Comment Insights
tools.description:
Analyze YouTube audience comments for a niche.

Use mode="discover" to find recurring audience questions/content requests and recurring dislikes or pain points. Use mode="validate" with idea to test one proposed video idea. Validation separates direct evidence from adjacent needs and reports sparse evidence as insufficient, not as proof the idea is bad. Always pass 'niche' (and 'idea') in English — the channel taxonomy is English-only, so a non-English niche finds no channels; translate the user's niche to English and put the audience language in 'language' (e.g. niche="PC gaming", language="pl"). Omit language to search across all channel languages.

This runs asynchronously: it returns an `mcpJobId` immediately. Poll `vidiq_job_poll` with that id until it is completed. Failed or expired jobs are refunded automatically.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

mode.description: discover finds recurring audience requests and pain points; validate tests one supplied idea.

niche.description: YouTube niche or topic used to select a semantic cohort of relevant active channels. ALWAYS pass this in English (the channel niche taxonomy is English-only, so a non-English niche selects no channels) — if the user names the niche in another language, translate it to the English equivalent (e.g. 'Gry komputerowe' -> 'PC gaming', 'cocina' -> 'cooking'). Put the audience language in the separate `language` field, not here. Do not pass a channel handle or URL.

idea.description: Required only for validate mode. The specific video idea to test; it must add a proposition beyond the niche. Pass in English.

language.description: Optional two-letter language for the returned comment evidence (e.g. 'pl' for Polish comments). This is where the audience language goes — keep `niche` in English and set the language here. Omit to analyze all languages.

mcpJobId.description: Opaque job id. Pass this to `vidiq_job_poll` to check progress and get the result.

status.description: Always 'inprogress' on submit — the work runs asynchronously.

message.description: Human-readable next-step instruction for the caller.

tools.name: vidiq_video_earnings_estimate
tools.title: Estimate Video Earnings
tools.description:
Estimate a single YouTube video's ad-revenue earnings as a low/mid/high range in USD.

Give it a video id or URL. It resolves whether the video is long-form or a Short, looks up the channel's category and country, and applies vidIQ's RPM model (category RPM x geo multiplier, with a much lower RPM for Shorts).

Use this to answer "how much did/does this video earn?".

Important: this is a rough estimate, not exact. It assumes the channel is monetized, uses the channel's country as a proxy for viewer geography, and counts all views as ad-serving. Channels under ~1,000 subscribers are usually not monetized.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

videoId.description: A YouTube video id (e.g. 'dQw4w9WgXcQ') or any YouTube video URL (watch, youtu.be, /shorts/, /embed/, /live/)

tools.name: vidiq_earnings_calculate
tools.title: Calculate Earnings From Views
tools.description:
Calculate estimated monthly YouTube earnings (low/mid/high USD) for a given number of monthly views.

This is a calculator, not a lookup: it does not fetch anything from YouTube, so you must supply the numbers. Use it for "how much would X views/month earn?", what-if scenarios, and niche/geo comparisons. To price a real, existing video by id or URL, use vidiq_video_earnings_estimate instead.

Set subject to 'video' for one video (then format 'long' or 'short' is required) or 'channel' for a channel's mixed output (then shortsShare is the fraction of views that are Shorts, default 0 = all long-form). Content format and the supplied context can significantly affect the estimate, so provide accurate inputs and ask the user when the format or mix is unknown.

Provide category, country, language, and subscriberCount when known. The result is an estimate, not the channel's actual revenue.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

subject.description: What the monthly views belong to: 'video' (a single video, so it is either long-form or a Short) or 'channel' (a mix, so pass shortsShare)

monthlyViews.description: Monthly views to price (the estimate returned is monthly)

category.description: Content category. Providing the accurate category improves the estimate

format.description: Video format. Required when subject is 'video'; must be omitted when subject is 'channel' (use shortsShare instead). Content format significantly affects the estimate

shortsShare.description: Channel only: fraction of monthly views that are Shorts (0.3 = 30%). Defaults to 0. Content mix significantly affects the estimate

country.description: ISO-3166 alpha-2 country of the audience or channel

language.description: Content language. Use an ISO-639-1 code or a locale tag such as en-US

subscriberCount.description: Channel subscriber count, when known. Providing it improves the estimate

tools.name: vidiq_video_stats
tools.title: Video Stats History
tools.description:
Get historical statistics for a YouTube video over time, including views, likes, comments, and views per hour (VPH).

Use this tool to:
- Track how a video's performance changes over time
- Compare view velocity (VPH) across different periods
- Analyze engagement trends (likes, comments) for a specific video

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

granularity.description: Time granularity for stats data points

tools.name: vidiq_video_change_history
tools.title: Video Change History
tools.description:
Get the observed title and thumbnail change history for one YouTube video.

Each change records when a title or thumbnail edit was observed. Thumbnail entries include the original YouTube URL and vidIQ's archived snapshot URL. The response also includes observed thumbnail A/B tests and their variants.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

tools.name: vidiq_get_videos_by_ids
tools.title: Get Videos by IDs
tools.description:
Get detailed metadata for one or more YouTube videos.

Use this tool to:
- Fetch video details such as title, description, tags, and category
- Get current statistics (views, likes, comments) for specific videos
- Look up publishing info, channel details, and thumbnails for videos
- Check topic categories for videos

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

videoIds.description: One to 50 YouTube video IDs or URLs

tools.name: vidiq_youtube_search
tools.title: Search YouTube
tools.description:
Search all of YouTube for videos, channels, or playlists matching a query, with optional filters (topic, region, publish date, duration, channel). Use this when someone asks to "find videos about X", "search YouTube for Y", "find channels about Z", or wants results for a specific keyword.

Unlike vidiq_trending_videos (which returns what's hot right now) and vidiq_outliers (which finds videos over-performing relative to their channel), this is a general keyword search across the whole catalog. It returns raw YouTube search results, NOT keyword metrics — for search volume/competition use keyword research instead.

Use this tool to:
- Find videos, channels, or playlists by keyword (set 'type')
- Narrow results by topic, region, publish-date window, and (for videos) duration, definition (HD), or live/upcoming event type
- Search within a single channel by passing 'channelId'
- Sort by relevance, recency ('date'), or popularity ('viewCount')

Filters marked "Video only" require type='video'.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

type.description: Kinds of result to return — any combination of video, channel, playlist. Defaults to all three. The video-only filters require type to be exactly ['video'].

order.description: Sort order. 'date' = newest, 'viewCount' = most viewed, 'videoCount' = channels with most videos.

publishedAfter.description: Only results published after this RFC 3339 timestamp (e.g. '2026-01-01T00:00:00Z')

publishedBefore.description: Only results published before this RFC 3339 timestamp

channelId.description: Restrict the search to a channel ID, @handle, or YouTube channel URL

regionCode.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 region code to localize results (e.g. 'US', 'DE')

videoDuration.description: Length: short (<4min), medium (4-20min), long (>20min). Video only.

id.description: YouTube id of the video, channel, or playlist (depending on kind)

channelId.description: Channel id associated with this result, when available

viewCount.description: Current view count. For videos this is video views; for channels this is total channel views.

duration.description: Video duration as an ISO 8601 duration, video results only

likeCount.description: Current video likes, video results only

commentCount.description: Current video comments, video results only

subscriberCount.description: Subscriber count for the result's channel, when public and available

vph.description: Views per hour from vidiq outlier/trend data, video results only

outlierScore.description: Outlier score from vidiq outlier data, video results only

tools.name: vidiq_get_channels_by_ids
tools.title: Get Channels by IDs
tools.description:
Get detailed information about YouTube channels by their IDs.

Use this tool to:
- Look up channel metadata (title, description, country) for one or more channels
- Get subscriber counts, view counts, and video counts
- Retrieve channel tags and topic categories
- Check channel thumbnails

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

channelIds.description: List of YouTube channel IDs to look up

tools.name: vidiq_balance
tools.title: Credits Balance
tools.description:
Check the user's current vidIQ credits balance.

vidIQ credits live in two buckets:
- A renewable bucket sized by the user's plan (Free/Boost/Max/etc) that refills each billing cycle.
- Zero or more add-on (bonus) credits. Add-on credits drain alongside renewable credits but do NOT refill.

Field semantics are in the output schema. Key invariant: totalCredits = renewableCredits + addOnCredits; maxRenewableCredits is the plan cap only.

Example — Boost user with an open promo grant:
  { type: 'limited', totalCredits: 1800,
    renewableCredits: 1500, maxRenewableCredits: 2000,
    renewableResetsAt: '2026-06-01T00:00:00Z',
    addOnCredits: 300, maxAddOnCredits: 500 }
Read as: 1,800 left = 1,500 of 2,000 renewable + 300 of a 500-credit bonus pool. Renews Jun 1.

Cost: 0 credit(s) per call.

type.description: 'limited' means the user has a finite renewable credit budget that refills each billing cycle. 'unlimited' means the user is on an unlimited plan (e.g. enterprise) and the renewable bucket does not decrement.

totalCredits.description: Total remaining credits the user can spend right now — renewableCredits plus addOnCredits. Null when type='unlimited'. This is the headline number to show in chat.

renewableCredits.description: Remaining credits in the renewable plan bucket alone — does NOT include add-on credits. Null when type='unlimited'.

maxRenewableCredits.description: The user's renewable plan cap (e.g. 150 for Free, 2000 for Boost, 6000 for Max). This is the amount that refills each billing cycle. Does NOT include add-on credits. Null when the plan has no cap.

renewableResetsAt.description: ISO timestamp when the renewable credit bucket next renews. Add-on credits do NOT renew; only the renewable bucket. Null when type='unlimited' or the backend did not return a renewal time.

addOnCredits.description: Remaining add-on (bonus) credits. Drain alongside renewable credits and do NOT refill on the billing cycle.

maxAddOnCredits.description: Initial total of all currently-active add-on credits — i.e. how much bonus credit the user originally received. Combine with addOnCredits to compute add-on usage.

tools.name: vidiq_user_channels
tools.title: User Channels
tools.description:
Get the list of YouTube channels authorized by the current user.

The response includes `authenticatedAs` (the email of the connected vidIQ account).
An empty `channels` list usually means the user authorized a different account than
they expected — tell them which account they're connected as and suggest reconnecting
with the intended one rather than treating it as an error.

Cost: 0 credit(s) per call.

authenticatedAs.description: Email of the vidIQ account this MCP connection is authenticated as. When the channel list looks wrong or empty, surface this so the user can confirm they connected the intended account.

tools.name: vidiq_user_videos
tools.title: User Videos
tools.description:
List videos from one of the current user's directly authorized YouTube channels through the authenticated vidIQ MCP connection, including public, unlisted, and private videos.

Use vidiq_user_channels when the channel ID is unknown. Supports privacy, video-type, title-search, ordering, limit, and cursor filters. Use vidiq_channel_videos for arbitrary public channels. Do not fall back to public results when channel authorization fails.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

channelId.description: Canonical YouTube channel ID owned by the current user. Call vidiq_user_channels if unknown.

privacyStatus.description: Video privacy filters. Defaults to public, unlisted, and private videos.

videoType.description: Video type filters. Omit when all long, short, and live videos are acceptable.

search.description: Optional title-only search string, from 1 to 100 characters.

pageToken.description: Opaque cursor returned by a previous call with the same filters.

tools.name: vidiq_channel_videos
tools.title: Channel Videos
tools.description:
Get videos from a YouTube channel by format (long-form, Shorts, or live streams). Use this when you already know which channel to look at. To discover videos across many channels, use vidiq_outliers or vidiq_trending_videos.

Use vidiq_user_videos instead when the user needs their owned-channel library, private or unlisted videos, title search, privacy filters, or cursor pagination.

Use this tool to:
- Browse a channel's recent uploads by video type (popular=false)
- Discover a channel's most popular videos by type (popular=true, default)
- Compare current views, likes, comments, views per hour (VPH), and breakout scores
- Get video metadata including titles, publish dates, thumbnails, and durations

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

videoFormat.description: Type of videos to retrieve: 'long' for long-form, 'short' for Shorts, 'live' for live streams

popular.description: When true (default), returns the most popular videos. When false, returns recent uploads.

channelThumbnail.description: YouTube channel avatar thumbnail URL, or null if unavailable

viewCount.description: Current YouTube view count, or null if unavailable

likeCount.description: Current YouTube like count, or null if unavailable

commentCount.description: Current YouTube comment count, or null if unavailable

duration.description: Video duration in ISO-8601 format (for example, 'PT12M34S'), or null if unavailable

vph.description: Current views per hour, or null if unavailable

breakoutScore.description: Performance relative to the channel's typical videos, or null if unavailable

tools.name: vidiq_video_transcript
tools.title: Video Transcript
tools.description:
Get the full transcript (captions) of a YouTube video.

Use this tool to:
- Analyze what a video talks about without watching it
- Extract key topics, quotes, or timestamps from a video
- Compare content across multiple videos by reading their transcripts
- Research video content for SEO or content strategy purposes

When a language is requested, this tool never silently substitutes captions in another language.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

videoId.description: YouTube video ID (e.g. 'dQw4w9WgXcQ') or a YouTube video URL

language.description: Requested transcript language as a BCP-47 code (e.g. 'en', 'es', 'pt-BR'). When supplied, only a matching caption track is returned; omit it to use the video's default captions.

tools.name: vidiq_video_comments
tools.title: Video Comments
tools.description:
Get YouTube comment threads for a video or channel, including replies.

Provide exactly one of videoId or channelId.

Each returned thread carries the videoId and videoTitle it belongs to, so channel-wide results can be attributed to individual videos. Either field is omitted when YouTube does not report it or the video's metadata is unavailable.

Use this tool to:
- Understand audience sentiment and reactions to a video
- Find common questions or feedback themes in comments
- Browse recent comments across an entire channel
- Identify the most liked or discussed comments

Paging and filtering: maxResult is the upstream page size, and minLikes filters that page by top-level comment likes. A page can therefore come back with fewer threads than maxResult, or with none at all, while more matches still exist. Each page is a separate charged call, so do not sweep to exhaustion by default: fetch another page with the returned nextPageToken (same filters) only while you still need more evidence and the caller's budget allows, and stop as soon as you have enough. A null nextPageToken means the upstream corpus is exhausted and there is nothing left to read.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

videoId.description: YouTube video ID (e.g. 'dQw4w9WgXcQ'). Provide either videoId or channelId.

channelId.description: YouTube channel ID, handle (e.g. '@MrBeast'), or channel URL. Provide either videoId or channelId.

maxResult.description: Upstream page size: how many comment threads are fetched per call (1–100). When minLikes is set, fewer threads than this can be returned because filtering is applied to the fetched page only — request another page with nextPageToken if the matches so far are not enough.

minLikes.description: Optional inclusive like threshold on the top-level comment: keep only threads whose top-level comment has at least this many likes. Replies of kept threads are not filtered. Omit (or 0) to return every thread.

pageToken.description: Opaque cursor from a previous call's nextPageToken. Pass the same videoId/channelId, order, and minLikes when continuing.

videoId.description: ID of the video this thread belongs to. Omitted when YouTube did not report one.

videoTitle.description: Title of the video this thread belongs to. Omitted when the video's metadata is unavailable (e.g. deleted or private).

tools.name: vidiq_channel_performance_trends
tools.title: Channel Video Performance Trends
tools.description:
Get a channel's typical video performance curve — how views accumulate over time after publication.

Returns statistical aggregates (min, max, avg, median, percentiles) of view counts at various time intervals since publication, based on the channel's recent videos.

Use this tool to:
- Understand how quickly a channel's videos gain views after publishing
- Compare a channel's view velocity against benchmarks
- Identify whether a channel has strong initial traction or slow-burn growth

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

channelId.description: YouTube channel ID, handle (e.g. '@MrBeast'), or channel URL

tools.name: vidiq_channel_analytics
tools.title: Channel Analytics
tools.description:
Get YouTube Analytics data for a channel you own — views, watch time, subscribers gained, likes, comments, retention, traffic sources, demographics, and revenue (monetized channels).

Common reports are available as one-word presets via `report`: audience_retention (per-video drop-off curve), traffic_sources, audience_demographics, audience_geography, revenue_report, top_videos, shorts_vs_longform_split. Or build custom queries with flexible date ranges, metric selection, and dimensional breakdowns (by day, country, device type, traffic source, etc.).

Use this tool to:
- Analyze channel performance over a specific time period
- See where viewers drop off in a video (report='audience_retention' + filters='video==VIDEO_ID')
- Break down views by traffic source, country, device type, age/gender
- See which videos actually earn (report='revenue_report', dimensions=['video'])
- Compare Shorts vs long-form performance (report='shorts_vs_longform_split')

Note: Only available for channels authorized to your account. Revenue metrics additionally require the channel to be monetized.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

report.description: Named report preset that fills metrics/dimensions/sort with a known-good YouTube Analytics report shape (explicitly-passed metrics/dimensions/sort/maxResults still win). audience_retention: per-video retention curve — REQUIRES filters='video==VIDEO_ID'. traffic_sources: views by source (search, suggested, browse, external...). audience_demographics: age/gender split (viewerPercentage). audience_geography: views by country. revenue_report: daily earnings (monetized channels only; combine with dimensions=['video'] for per-video earnings — YouTube does not support revenue by traffic source). top_videos: own videos ranked by views (pass sort='-estimatedRevenue' plus revenue metrics to rank by earnings instead). shorts_vs_longform_split: views/watch-time split between Shorts, long-form and live (creatorContentType).

startDate.description: Start date (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to 28 days ago

metrics.description: Metrics to retrieve. Default: views, estimatedMinutesWatched, subscribersGained, likes, comments. Some dimensions support only a restricted metric set — an unsupported metric is rejected, and omitted metrics narrow to the supported subset of the default. Each restricted dimension and the metrics it allows: insightTrafficSourceType, insightTrafficSourceDetail, insightPlaybackLocationType, insightPlaybackLocationDetail, deviceType → views, estimatedMinutesWatched, averageViewDuration, averageViewPercentage; subscribedStatus → those plus likes, dislikes, annotationClickThroughRate; ageGroup, gender → viewerPercentage; elapsedVideoTimeRatio → audienceWatchRatio, relativeRetentionPerformance, totalSegmentImpressions. For subscriber/comment metrics use a time/geo dimension (day, country).

dimensions.description: Dimensions to break down by (e.g. day, country, deviceType). month: startDate/endDate are snapped to the first of their month (YouTube requires month-aligned bounds). video, insightTrafficSourceDetail, insightPlaybackLocationDetail are top-N reports (ranked by views; pass sort/maxResults to change); the two *Detail dims also need a parent-type filter (insightTrafficSourceType== / insightPlaybackLocationType==), and those filters are valid only with their matching *Detail dimension. elapsedVideoTimeRatio (audience retention) needs a video== filter. Most dimensions can't be combined (YouTube supports only specific report shapes) — if a combo is rejected, request each dimension separately.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of rows to return. insightTrafficSourceDetail and insightPlaybackLocationDetail allow at most 25 (default 25); video allows at most 200 (default 25); elapsedVideoTimeRatio requires at least 100 (default 100) because audience retention is a 100-point curve and does not have the video's 200-row ceiling.

sort.description: Sort field, prefix with '-' for descending (e.g. '-views')

tools.name: vidiq_subscriber_insights
tools.title: Subscriber Insights
tools.description:
Analyze subscriber overlap and best times to post for a YouTube channel you own.

Returns the channels most commonly subscribed to by your audience, dated overlap history, and a timezone-adjusted histogram of sampled public YouTube activity with the strongest three-hour windows. The activity signal is not watch history or live online-presence data. Only channels authorized to your account are allowed.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

channelId.description: An owned YouTube channel ID, handle, or channel URL

timezoneOffset.description: Whole-hour UTC offset used for the activity histogram: Z or ±HH:00. Fractional-hour offsets are rejected because the current upstream truncates them.

limit.description: Maximum number of audience-overlap channels to return (1-50)

growthUpdatedAt.description: When growth history was updated, or null when growth data is unavailable.

tools.name: vidiq_trend_categories
tools.title: Trend Categories
tools.description:
List all available trend category slugs with display names and descriptions. Use this as a reference before filtering outlier videos by trend category.

Cost: 0 credit(s) per call.

tools.name: vidiq_similar_channels
tools.title: Similar Channels
tools.description:
Find COMPETITORS of a channel — either the user's own channel or a specific named channel. Uses neural semantic search tuned for competitor matching; the user's own authorized channels are automatically excluded from legacy manual-mode results.

Use this tool ONLY when someone asks for competitors or similar channels relative to a channel:
- "Who are my competitors?" or "Find channels like mine" (the user's own channel — country/language are auto-detected in manual mode)
- "Channels similar to [channel]", "Competitors of [channel]", or "Channels like @handle" (a named reference channel)

Do NOT use this tool for generic channel discovery by topic, size, growth, or any other criteria ("find tech review channels", "top gaming channels in Brazil", "fastest growing fitness channels") — use vidiq_channel_search for that.

Choose exactly one mode: channelId or niche.

ADDITIVE CHANNEL ID MODE — when a canonical YouTube channel ID beginning with UC was supplied or already resolved, pass only channelId, plus optional size and sort. Do not copy resolved channel characteristics into this request or add niche/manual filters. Do not call vidiq_channel_search when a canonical ID is already available. A handle or URL must be resolved externally to a canonical channel ID before using this mode. The API derives the source classification and search tuning and excludes the reference channel.

LEGACY MANUAL NICHE MODE — Legacy manual niche behavior is unchanged. The niche parameter is required in this mode — always provide a clear topic or content theme. All existing manual inputs remain supported, including minSubscribers, maxSubscribers, avgViews, avgViewsMin, avgViewsMax, country, language, channelType, faceless, and excludeChannelIds.

SIMILAR TO A SPECIFIC CHANNEL IN LEGACY MANUAL MODE — when using the existing manual path, do NOT guess the reference channel's characteristics. Supply the same fields as before:
- niche: the reference channel's niche + subNiches, comma-separated (e.g. 'YouTube Growth, Monetization & SEO')
- country: the reference channel's country
- language: the first code from the reference channel's languages
- channelType: the reference channel's channelType
- faceless: the reference channel's isFaceless value
- minSubscribers / maxSubscribers: a band around its subscriberCount, roughly 10% as min and 5x as max, unless the user asks for a specific range
- avgViews: the reference channel's avgViews; do not also set avgViewsMin/avgViewsMax unless the user asks for a specific range
- excludeChannelIds: the reference channel's channelId

Omit sort for normal similarity ranking. When the user asks to rank these competitors by size or recent growth, set sort to subscriberCount, subsGrowth30d, or viewsGrowth30d; all explicit sorts reorder only the requested top similarity results.

Results include the metrics used for sorting plus channel type and faceless status. In manual niche mode, country is a ranking preference rather than a strict filter, while language filters the language channels publish in. When omitted, country and language are auto-detected from the user's authorized channel.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

channelId.description: Canonical YouTube channel ID beginning with UC. It is passed directly to the Similar Channels API without a resolution request.

niche.description: Manual niche, topic, or content theme to search in. Use natural language — e.g. 'tech reviews' or 'vegan cooking tutorials'. Provide either this or channelId, not both; prefer channelId for a specific reference channel.

minSubscribers.description: Lower bound for subscriber count. Use to filter out smaller channels — e.g. 10000 to only see channels with 10k+ subscribers. Use together with maxSubscribers to define a specific range.

maxSubscribers.description: Upper bound for subscriber count. Use to filter out larger channels — e.g. 1000000 to cap results at channels under 1M subscribers. Use together with minSubscribers to define a specific range.

avgViews.description: The reference channel's lifetime average views per video (total views / total videos). When searching for competitors of a specific channel, pass its avgViews here so results are auto-ranged to a similar per-video-views league (parallels passing the reference channel's subscriber band). Leave unset for generic niche searches.

avgViewsMin.description: Manual lower bound for lifetime average views per video (total views / total videos), overriding the avgViews auto-range. Use to require results that average at least this many views per video — e.g. 50000 for '50k+ average views'. This is the per-video average, not total views.

avgViewsMax.description: Manual upper bound for lifetime average views per video (total views / total videos), overriding the avgViews auto-range. Use together with avgViewsMin to define a specific per-video average-views range.

country.description: Two-letter ISO 3166-1 country code used to prefer channels BASED IN that country — e.g. 'US', 'GB', 'BR', 'JP'. Matching channels receive a ranking boost, but channels based elsewhere may still appear. This is where the channel is located — NOT the audience/viewer country, and NOT the channel's language (use `language` to filter by language). When omitted, the country is auto-detected from the user's authorized channel (if any).

language.description: Two-letter ISO 639-1 language code to filter results to channels whose content is in that language — e.g. 'en', 'es', 'pt', 'ja'. Pass the user's requested content language here (the language the channel publishes in — this is the channel's language, not its country). Only a single language is accepted. When omitted, the language is auto-detected from the user's authorized channel (if any).

channelType.description: Reference channel format. 'long' prefers long and mixed candidates; 'short' prefers short and mixed candidates; 'mixed' is neutral. This affects ranking, not eligibility.

faceless.description: Reference channel faceless status. When provided, candidates with the same status receive a ranking boost; other candidates remain eligible.

sort.description: Optional descending sort of the requested top similarity results: subscriberCount, subsGrowth30d, or viewsGrowth30d. Omit to keep neural similarity relevance order.

size.description: Number of similar channels to return. Defaults to 30, maximum 50.

excludeChannelIds.description: Manual niche mode only: channel IDs to exclude from results. The user's own authorized channels are excluded automatically and do not need to be listed.

tools.name: vidiq_similar_videos
tools.title: Similar Videos
tools.description:
Find high-performing YouTube videos similar to a seed video - the video-level counterpart of vidiq_similar_channels. Give it one video ID or URL and it returns videos ranked by combined similarity: textual (title/topic) and visual (thumbnail), fused with each video labeled by which signals matched (`matchedBy`; matching both earns a ranking boost). Use this for topic ideation ('find 50 videos like this outlier'), studying how a proven concept is packaged across channels, or expanding one winning video into a content cluster. Searches vidIQ's high-performing/outlier video index - results skew toward videos that overperform, which is what makes them useful as ideation references. Results are ordered most-similar-first; no numeric similarity score is exposed. Use `minEngagementRate` to filter copycat/re-upload spam around viral seeds. Check `signalsUsed`/`signalsFailed` before interpreting an empty result. For channel-level similarity use vidiq_similar_channels; for thumbnail-only search use vidiq_similar_thumbnails.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

videoId.description: Seed YouTube video: an 11-character video ID (e.g. 'dQw4w9WgXcQ') or a video URL. Results are videos similar to this one.

matchOn.description: Similarity signals to use. 'both' (default) fuses title/topic similarity with thumbnail visual similarity. 'title' uses only textual similarity (works for Shorts). 'thumbnail' uses only visual thumbnail similarity (long-form index only).

contentType.description: Filter results by format. Note: thumbnail similarity only covers long-form videos, so 'short' results come from title similarity alone.

minEngagementRate.description: Minimum engagement rate (likes/views, 0-1). Filters out low-engagement copycat/re-upload channels that flood results for viral seeds; real creators typically show 0.03-0.12, content farms 0.002-0.01. Recommended around 0.02 when seeding from a mega-viral video.

channelCountry.description: Restrict to channels BASED IN this country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, e.g. 'US', 'PL'). This is where the channel is located — NOT the audience/viewer country, and NOT the language of the videos.

excludeSeedChannel.description: Set true to drop videos from the seed video's own channel.

matchedBy.description: Which similarity signals matched this video. Matching both earns a rank-fusion boost.

signalsUsed.description: Signals whose search actually ran and contributed candidates. If a requested signal is missing here, its search did not run - do NOT conclude 'no similar videos exist' for that signal.

signalsFailed.description: Requested signals that could not run, with a stable public reason code.

tools.name: vidiq_submit_feedback
tools.title: Submit Feedback
tools.description:
Submit feedback about the vidIQ MCP — feature requests, bug reports, improvement suggestions, survey responses, or general comments. When the user encounters a bug with vidIQ MCP or requests a new vidIQ MCP feature, proactively ask whether they would like you to submit a bug report or feature request to vidIQ. Call this tool when the user explicitly asks to submit, send, record, or report feedback to vidIQ. Comments made while asking for help do not by themselves indicate submission intent. If submission intent is ambiguous, ask whether the user wants the feedback sent to vidIQ and wait for confirmation.

Cost: 0 credit(s) per call.

type.description: The kind of feedback: feature_request for new tools/capabilities, bug_report for something broken, improvement for enhancing an existing tool, survey_response for answers to a survey or research invitation, general for anything else

tool_name.description: The relevant existing tool name, if this feedback is about a specific tool (e.g. 'vidiq_keyword_research')

description.description: What you're requesting, reporting, or suggesting — and why

summary.description: Concise, searchable summary of this feedback (up to 500 characters)

campaign_id.description: Survey or campaign identifier provided in the invitation; omit for ordinary feedback

use_case.description: A specific workflow or scenario for additional context

tools.name: vidiq_score_title
tools.title: Score Title
tools.description:
Score a YouTube video title for click-through-rate potential. Returns a score (0-100) indicating how compelling and clickable the title is. Use this to compare title variations and pick the best-performing option.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

tools.name: vidiq_score_thumbnail
tools.title: Score Thumbnail
tools.description:
Score a YouTube video thumbnail for click-through-rate potential. Returns a score (0-100) with detailed feedback on strengths and improvements. Provide a video ID and title; optionally supply a custom thumbnail image URL to score instead of the current YouTube thumbnail.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

title.description: Video title (used together with the thumbnail for scoring)

image.description: Thumbnail image URL or an uploaded image. If omitted, the current YouTube thumbnail is used.

tools.name: vidiq_generate_titles
tools.title: Generate Titles
tools.description:
Generate scored YouTube title suggestions.

Provide at least one of `videoId`, `title`, or `description`. With
only `videoId`, the current title/description are fetched from YouTube.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

videoId.description: YouTube video ID (e.g. 'dQw4w9WgXcQ'). When provided, the tool fetches the current title/description from yt-proxy to ground generation. Optional when title and/or description are supplied directly.

title.description: Current/working video title. When omitted but videoId is provided, fetched from yt-proxy. Caller-supplied value takes precedence.

description.description: Current video description. When omitted but videoId is provided, fetched from yt-proxy. Caller-supplied value takes precedence.

numTitles.description: How many title candidates to generate (default: 3)

type.description: Video format hint. Affects the generation prompt and scoring rubric. When omitted, upstream infers from duration and otherwise treats the video as long-form.

language.description: Target language for generated titles and the analysis pass (e.g. 'en', 'pt-BR'). Defaults to English when omitted.

regionCode.description: 2-letter ISO country code (e.g. 'US', 'BR'). Normalized to uppercase. Used by upstream when fetching competitive context.

scoreThreshold.description: Return only suggestions with score >= threshold. Thresholds above 70 on long-form videos may legitimately yield no results, and the filter applies before the numTitles top-K slice (so the response may contain fewer items than numTitles).

previousTitles.description: Recent titles from the same channel. Used by upstream to reduce repetition and improve novelty. Capped at 20 entries x 200 chars; duplicates removed.

competitorTitles.description: Seed titles for the competitive context block. When provided, upstream skips its Outliers lookup and uses these directly — useful for deterministic output or when the caller already has a curated competitor set. Capped at 20 entries x 200 chars; duplicates removed.

analysisSummary.description: Pre-computed analysis summary. When provided, upstream skips its own analysis pass (transcript/frames → Gemini) and uses this directly. Useful when chaining after a tool that already produced video understanding. Capped at 4000 chars.

tools.name: vidiq_generate_comment_replies
tools.title: Generate YouTube Comment Replies
tools.description:
Generate multiple draft replies to one viewer comment on a YouTube video, with one reply per requested tone. Use this when the user wants response ideas for a specific comment. To retrieve comments first, use `vidiq_video_comments`.

Provide the video's title and the exact viewer comment. Optionally provide 3–10 tone labels; otherwise the defaults are General, Humorous, Thankful, Witty, and Informal.

This tool returns draft text only. It never posts or otherwise changes anything on YouTube.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

title.description: Title of the YouTube video that received the viewer comment.

comment.description: Viewer comment to draft replies for.

tones.description: Three to ten tone labels for the reply options. Defaults to General, Humorous, Thankful, Witty, and Informal.

items.description: Tone label to use for one reply option.

title.description: Video title used to generate the replies.

tone.description: Tone used for this generated reply.

reply.description: Generated reply text. Review it before posting to YouTube.

replies.description: Generated reply options, one per requested tone.

tools.name: vidiq_generate_thumbnail
tools.title: Generate Thumbnail
tools.description:
Generate a YouTube thumbnail.

Provide at least one of videoId, title, description, or userQuery. With only a videoId, the video's current
title, description, and thumbnail are pulled in automatically.

This runs asynchronously: it returns an `mcpJobId` immediately. Poll `vidiq_job_poll` with that id until
it is "completed" to get the thumbnail (shown inline) with its imageUrl, a self-score, and short feedback.
Credits are charged on submit and automatically refunded if generation fails.

Include the imageUrl in your reply so the user can open or save the file. The inline preview isn't downloadable.

Treat the score as a rough estimate rather than a verdict: don't lead with it, and don't regenerate just to
raise it. To iterate, change one thing at a time and keep the best result. For a reliable critique, use
vidiq_score_thumbnail.

Cost: 22 credit(s) per call.

videoId.description: YouTube video ID (e.g. 'dQw4w9WgXcQ'). When provided, title, description, and currentThumbnail are auto-filled from YouTube unless the caller supplies them explicitly. Optional when at least one of title, description, or userQuery is given.

title.description: Video title used for grounding. When omitted but videoId is provided, fetched from yt-proxy. Caller-supplied value wins.

description.description: Video description used for grounding. When omitted but videoId is provided, fetched from yt-proxy. Caller-supplied value wins.

transcript.description: Optional transcript text. Used for subject detection in Quick Generate and as context in Pro Generate. Pair with vidiq_video_transcript when available.

userQuery.description: Natural-language creative direction (e.g. 'show the host pointing at a glowing dollar sign'). Highest-priority generation signal upstream.

currentThumbnail.description: An existing/current thumbnail to reference for composition, a hosted image URL or an uploaded image. When omitted but videoId is provided, auto-filled with the best available resolution of the video's YouTube thumbnail.

subjectImage.description: A subject/person image, a hosted image URL or an uploaded image. Highest-priority likeness reference for the main face in the thumbnail.

referenceImages.description: Reference thumbnails to emulate style/composition, hosted image URLs or uploaded images. Presence of this field switches the request out of Quick Generate into the Pro / Improve flow upstream. Capped at 10 entries; duplicates removed.

orientation.description: Thumbnail orientation. 'landscape' is the standard 16:9 YouTube thumbnail (default when omitted); 'portrait' is a 9:16 Shorts thumbnail.

score.description: Overall quality score (0–100) returned by the previous scoring call.

pointImpact.description: Point delta this finding contributed to the overall score (when available).

strengths.description: Findings to preserve in the next iteration.

pointImpact.description: Point delta this finding contributed to the overall score (when available).

improvements.description: Findings to fix in the next iteration.

feedback.description: Optional scorer feedback from a prior thumbnail (typically the output of vidiq_score_thumbnail). When provided alongside referenceImages, triggers the feedback-iteration flow.

mcpJobId.description: Opaque job id. Pass this to `vidiq_job_poll` to check progress and get the result.

status.description: Always 'inprogress' on submit — the work runs asynchronously.

message.description: Human-readable next-step instruction for the caller.

tools.name: vidiq_refine_thumbnail
tools.title: Refine Thumbnail
tools.description:
Change or improve a YouTube thumbnail by describing what you want in plain words.

Give it the thumbnail to change as sourceThumbnail (a hosted URL) or sourceThumbnailFile (a ChatGPT upload),
and say what to change (instructions) — for example "make the text bigger" or "change the background to a
football stadium".

This runs asynchronously: it returns an `mcpJobId` immediately. Poll `vidiq_job_poll` with that id until
it is "completed" to get the updated thumbnail (shown inline) with its imageUrl. Credits are charged on
submit and automatically refunded if refinement fails.

Include the imageUrl in your reply so the user can open or save the file. The inline preview isn't downloadable.

Cost: 22 credit(s) per call.

sourceThumbnail.description: The thumbnail you want to change as a hosted image URL or base64 data URI. Usually this is the imageUrl from vidiq_generate_thumbnail. Use sourceThumbnailFile instead for a ChatGPT file upload.

sourceThumbnailFile.description: The thumbnail you want to change as a ChatGPT-uploaded file. Use this instead of sourceThumbnail when the user uploads the source image.

instructions.description: What you want changed, in plain words, for example 'make the background darker' or 'make the face bigger'. Describe the change, not the whole picture.

originalConcept.description: Optional. A short description of what the original thumbnail shows. Helps keep the result on-topic. If left out, your instructions are used.

videoId.description: Optional. The YouTube video this thumbnail is for.

subjectImage.description: Optional. A photo of the person who should be the main face in the thumbnail as a hosted image URL or base64 data URI.

referenceImages.description: Optional. Up to 10 hosted image URLs or base64 data URIs for thumbnails whose style you'd like to copy.

mask.description: Optional. To change only one area and leave the rest untouched, provide a base64 image that marks the area to change.

orientation.description: Thumbnail orientation. 'landscape' is the standard 16:9 YouTube thumbnail (default when omitted); 'portrait' is a 9:16 Shorts thumbnail. Ignored when a mask is supplied (mask edits keep the source dimensions).

mcpJobId.description: Opaque job id. Pass this to `vidiq_job_poll` to check progress and get the result.

status.description: Always 'inprogress' on submit — the work runs asynchronously.

message.description: Human-readable next-step instruction for the caller.

tools.name: vidiq_video_watch
tools.title: Watch Video
tools.description:
Watch a long-form YouTube video end-to-end and return a structured markdown walkthrough.

Use this tool to:
- Understand what happens visually in a video (not just what is said) — useful when transcripts miss context
- Generate scene-by-scene breakdowns with timestamps for editing or analysis
- Answer specific questions about a video by passing a custom `prompt`
- Compare visual structure across videos for SEO / hook research

This runs asynchronously: it returns an `mcpJobId` immediately. Poll `vidiq_job_poll` with that id until it is "completed" to get the markdown walkthrough in the `analysisText` field. Credits are charged on submit and automatically refunded if the analysis fails.

For short-form content, use `vidiq_watch_shortform_content` instead.

Note: prefer `vidiq_video_transcript` when you only need spoken words, since it is faster and cheaper.

Cost: 25 credit(s) per call.

video.description: Long-form YouTube video ID (e.g. 'dQw4w9WgXcQ') or watch/youtu.be URL. For short-form content, use vidiq_watch_shortform_content instead.

prompt.description: Optional custom analysis instruction. If omitted, a scene-by-scene markdown walkthrough is produced (### Scene N: Label headers with mm:ss timestamps + ### Summary bullets). Markdown structure is enforced regardless — do not ask for JSON.

mcpJobId.description: Opaque job id. Pass this to `vidiq_job_poll` to check progress and get the result.

status.description: Always 'inprogress' on submit — the work runs asynchronously.

message.description: Human-readable next-step instruction for the caller.

tools.name: vidiq_watch_shortform_content
tools.title: Watch Short-Form Content
tools.description:
Watch one piece of short-form content from Instagram, TikTok, or YouTube and return a markdown scene-by-scene walkthrough.

Pass the full public URL. For YouTube Shorts, a /shorts/, watch, or youtu.be URL is accepted; the content is verified to be short-form. Call this tool in parallel to compare multiple pieces of short-form content.

This runs asynchronously: it returns an `mcpJobId` immediately — poll `vidiq_job_poll` with that id until it is "completed" to get the walkthrough. Credits are charged on submit and automatically refunded if the analysis fails.

DO NOT USE FOR:
- Long-form YouTube videos — use `vidiq_video_watch`.
- TikTok short links (vm.tiktok.com or tiktok.com/t/) — paste the full /@user/video/<id> URL.
- Bare platform IDs or Instagram shortcodes — pass a full URL.

Cost: 10 credit(s) per call.

url.description: Full URL to short-form content on Instagram, TikTok, or YouTube. TikTok short links and bare platform IDs are not supported.

prompt.description: Optional custom analysis instruction. Omit it for the tuned scene-by-scene walkthrough. Markdown output only; do not ask for JSON.

mcpJobId.description: Opaque job id. Pass this to `vidiq_job_poll` to check progress and get the result.

status.description: Always 'inprogress' on submit — the work runs asynchronously.

message.description: Human-readable next-step instruction for the caller.

tools.name: vidiq_ig_profile
tools.title: Instagram Profile
tools.description:
Fetch public Instagram profile by handle: bio, follower/following counts, post count, verification, external URL, with the profile picture returned inline.

DO NOT USE FOR:
- Profile search/discovery — you must already have a handle.
- Reels — use `vidiq_ig_profile_reels` (up to 6, popularity-sorted, no pagination).
- Stories, Highlights, IGTV, private-account data.
- Engagement-rate or growth analytics — snapshot only.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

handle.description: Instagram handle (with or without leading @). 1-30 chars; letters/digits/dot/underscore.

tools.name: vidiq_ig_profile_reels
tools.title: Instagram Profile Reels
tools.description:
Fetch a creator's reels by handle: shortcode, caption, play/like/comment counts, duration, timestamp, pinned-profile status, with each reel's cover returned inline as an image. Returns up to 12 reels from the first Instagram Reels-tab page in Instagram's order: pinned reels first, then the remaining reels newest-first. Form a full Instagram reel URL from a returned shortcode before passing that short-form content URL to `vidiq_watch_shortform_content`.

DO NOT USE FOR:
- More than 12 reels, or pagination — not supported.
- Strict newest-first ordering across the whole response — older pinned reels may appear before newer unpinned reels.
- Image posts, carousels, Stories.
- Account, creator, influencer, or competitor-account discovery - use `vidiq_ig_accounts_from_outliers`.
- Cross-platform outlier examples or topic search - use `vidiq_instagram_tiktok_outlier_search` (cannot filter by handle).
- Watching or critiquing short-form content — use `vidiq_watch_shortform_content` with a full Instagram reel URL.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

handle.description: Instagram handle (with or without leading @). 1-30 chars; letters/digits/dot/underscore.

tools.name: vidiq_instagram_publish_reel
tools.title: Publish Instagram Reel
tools.description:
Publish an approved hosted MP4 using this same tool across short calls. First obtain approval for the exact video, account, caption and regular or Trial settings. Select a connected account with publishingAvailable=true. Start with videoUrl (use vidiq_video_upload for attachments); retain the returned containerId and platformAccountId. Continue with containerId and the same account, omitting videoUrl/caption/trialParams. The backend checks readiness and publishes when ready. IN_PROGRESS means wait about five seconds and call again. PUBLISHED confirms success; show permalink when available. Stop on any error; do not automatically retry failed calls or create a replacement. Continue processing checks for up to five minutes. The caller retains progress; closing the conversation pauses continuation. No YouTube channel or MFA is required. Continuation calls are free.

Cost: 0 credit(s) to start; continuation calls are free.

videoUrl.description: Chosen hosted MP4 URL to start preparation. Provide exactly one of videoUrl or containerId.

containerId.description: Meta ID returned by this tool. Continue the same container; do not create a replacement.

platformAccountId.description: Selected connected Instagram account; retain the same account for continuation calls.

caption.description: Exact caption including hashtags, only when starting with videoUrl; omit for no caption.

trialParams.description: Only when starting: omit for a regular Reel, or explicitly choose MANUAL or SS_PERFORMANCE for a Trial Reel.

tools.name: vidiq_instagram_connected_accounts
tools.title: My Connected Instagram Accounts
tools.description:
List the signed-in user's Instagram accounts already connected to vidIQ. Use this first when the user says "my Instagram", "my account", or otherwise asks about their own Instagram data.

Each account says whether private owner insights and Reel publishing are available. Publishing permission is independent of insights permission. If publishingAvailable is false, connect or reauthorize Instagram at https://app.vidiq.com using the existing account connection flow and refresh this list. For `accessLevel: "owner"`, call `vidiq_instagram_owner_insights` with that exact `platformAccountId`. For `accessLevel: "public_fallback"`, private insights are unavailable; if `username` is present, `vidiq_ig_profile_reels` may be used for public Reel data, and the response must be described as public rather than owner insights.

Do not use this tool to search arbitrary Instagram handles or to connect, refresh, or repair Instagram OAuth.

Cost: 0 credit(s) per call.

publishingAvailable.description: Active OAuth connection with Instagram publishing permission; Trial eligibility is checked by Instagram at publication time.

tools.name: vidiq_instagram_owner_insights
tools.title: My Instagram Owner Insights
tools.description:
Fetch private Instagram owner insights for an OAuth-backed account already connected to the signed-in vidIQ user. Always obtain `platformAccountId` from `vidiq_instagram_connected_accounts`; do not pass a handle or an account belonging to another user.

The Reel fields align with `vidiq_ig_profile_reels` where they mean the same thing, while owner-only metrics add shares, saves, watch time, watched percentage, skip rate, and `isPossibleTrial`. Instagram may delay owner metrics, so nullable values mean unavailable—not zero. `videoUrl` and `isPinned` are null because the owner-insights source does not provide those public fields.

If this returns `status: "unavailable"` and the connected-account result supplied a username, public Reel data may be fetched separately with `vidiq_ig_profile_reels`. Clearly disclose that fallback as public data. Do not claim public metrics are owner insights.

Cost: 0 credit(s) per call.

platformAccountId.description: Exact platformAccountId returned by vidiq_instagram_connected_accounts; never a username.

tools.name: vidiq_instagram_tiktok_outlier_search
tools.title: Instagram and TikTok Outliers
tools.description:
Search Instagram Reels and TikTok videos together for posts that substantially outperform each creator's median. Results are returned in separate Instagram and TikTok sections because relevance scores are not comparable across platforms.

Use `concept` for a complete content premise, `hook` for the first three seconds, or `format` for a subject-free production template. `audienceQuery` is a separate top-level audience rescore and must use: `Culture/Region: ...; Global: <true|false>; Demographics: ...;`.

Defaults to the last 30 days, English captions, at least 10K views, one result per creator within each platform, and 5 results per platform. `resultsPerPlatform` controls each section independently. Use at least two outliers from a platform before calling something a pattern. Use `vidiq_ig_accounts_from_outliers` instead for Instagram account discovery.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

audienceQuery.description: Required audience-rescore context as one string using `Culture/Region: ...; Global: <true|false>; Demographics: ...;`. Example: `Culture/Region: UK/British; Global: false; Demographics: working professional men 25-45, fat loss, busy lifestyle;`

excludeContentIds.description: Instagram reel shortcodes or TikTok video IDs to exclude.

excludeCreatorHandles.description: Creator handles to exclude from both platform searches, matched independently and without the leading @. Example: ["creator_one", "creator.two"].

resultsPerPlatform.description: Number of results to return from each platform.

tools.name: vidiq_ig_accounts_from_outliers
tools.title: Instagram Accounts From Outliers
tools.description:
Find Instagram creator/account candidates from existing outlier reel discovery.

Use this when the user asks for Instagram accounts, creators, competitors, influencers, partners, or examples to study. The service groups outlier reels into accounts and verifies candidates against profile and recent content.

How to call:
- `niche`: one-line content/account niche. Keep it about the creator's content, not audience demographics.
- `audienceQuery`: required audience context in this format: `Culture/Region: ...; Global: <true|false>; Demographics: ...;`
  Derive it from the user's stated target audience or profile/recent reels, not from handle alone. If audience is vague, ask before searching.
- Use optional `followersMin` / `followersMax` when account size matters.

Cost: 10 credit(s) per call.

niche.description: One-line description of the Instagram reel/content niche to search for.

tools.name: vidiq_list_competitors
tools.title: List Competitors
tools.description:
List the YouTube channels the user is tracking as competitors of one of their own channels.

Returns only channel IDs. To get titles, thumbnails, subscriber counts, etc., pass the IDs to vidiq_get_channels_by_ids.

The youtubeChannelId must be a channel the user has authorized — use vidiq_user_channels to discover them.

Cost: 0 credit(s) per call.

tools.name: vidiq_bookmarks_list
tools.title: List Bookmarks
tools.description:
List the signed-in user's saved bookmarks, newest first. Returns stored payloads, not live metrics. Pass nextOffset as offset for the next page; null means no more results.

Cost: 0 credit(s) per call.

tools.name: vidiq_bookmarks_save
tools.title: Save Bookmarks
tools.description:
Save 1–50 bookmarks of one type to the signed-in account in one atomic batch. Only save items the user explicitly asked to save; otherwise ask first. Repeated saves create duplicates. Do not automatically retry a failed save; inspect saved bookmarks first if the outcome is uncertain.

Cost: 0 credit(s) per call.

tags.description: Existing tag IDs applied to every item.

payloads.description: 1–50 payloads matching the current schema for this bookmarkType. Follow the field descriptions in this tool's input to build each payload.

tools.name: vidiq_bookmarks_remove
tools.title: Remove Bookmarks
tools.description:
Remove 1–50 bookmarks from the signed-in account in one atomic batch. Only remove items the user explicitly asked to remove; otherwise ask first. Duplicate IDs count once. Any unknown, already removed, or foreign ID rejects the entire batch. If the outcome is uncertain, inspect saved bookmarks before retrying.

Cost: 0 credit(s) per call.

tools.name: vidiq_update_competitors
tools.title: Update Competitors
tools.description:
Follow or unfollow competitor channels for one of the user's own YouTube channels.

- youtubeChannelId must be a channel the user has authorized (call vidiq_user_channels to discover).
- follow / unfollow are arrays of YouTube channel IDs — they must not overlap; at least one must be non-empty.
- Plan-based caps apply. Adding above the cap fails. Returns the resulting tracked-competitors list (channel IDs only).

Example arguments: { "youtubeChannelId": "UCowner123", "follow": ["UCcompA"], "unfollow": [] }

Cost: 0 credit(s) per call.

youtubeChannelId.description: YouTube channel ID (starts with 'UC', e.g. 'UCabc123') of one of the user's own authorized channels. Call vidiq_user_channels first if unknown.

follow.description: Array of YouTube channel IDs to start tracking as competitors, e.g. ["UCabc123","UCdef456"].

unfollow.description: Array of YouTube channel IDs to stop tracking, e.g. ["UCabc123"].

tools.name: vidiq_authorize_with_youtube
tools.title: Authorize with YouTube
tools.description:
Check or establish fresh YouTube authorization for the current vidIQ OAuth connection.

Call this tool when the user asks to authorize with YouTube, before a sensitive workflow that requires fresh YouTube authentication, or after the user completes the authorization handoff. It authorizes using a YouTube channel already connected to vidIQ; it does not connect a new channel. When authorization is required, show the authorization widget and wait for the user to use its controls.

Cost: 0 credit(s) per call.

tools.name: vidiq_update_video
tools.title: Update YouTube Video
tools.description:
Update metadata or publishing settings for a YouTube video owned by the user.

Supported updates match the vidIQ web app: title, description, complete tag list, privacy status, and scheduled publish time. Omitted fields remain unchanged. An empty description clears the description, and an empty tags array clears all tags. Thumbnail updates use a separate endpoint and are not supported by this tool.

Call this write tool only after the user explicitly chooses the exact channel, video, and final values to publish. Do not call it merely to preview, recommend, score, or draft changes. The channel must be directly authorized with owner access (call vidiq_user_channels if unknown), and the current vidIQ OAuth token must include YouTube verification.

When the result status is verification_required, show the verification widget and wait for the user to use its controls. Do not retry the video update until the user confirms verification is complete.

Cost: 5 credit(s) per call.

videoId.description: The YouTube video ID to update.

title.description: The exact final YouTube title to publish, from 1 to 100 characters.

tools.name: vidiq_generate_broll
tools.title: Find Stock B-roll
tools.description:
Find free stock B-roll video clips.

Provide a search query (optionally orientation and min/max duration filters).
Returns up to 4 clips with a direct mp4 link, a preview image, dimensions, and the
photographer credit. Attribution is required: always credit the photographer and

tools.name: vidiq_voiceover_list_voices
tools.title: List Voiceover Voices
tools.description:
List the available voiceover voices.

Returns each voice's id, name, category, description, and an optional audio preview URL.
The user's own cloned/designed voices have isCustom=true and are listed first; prefer
them when the user asks for "my voice". Use the returned voiceId with vidiq_voiceover_generate.

Cost: 0 credit(s) per call.

voiceId.description: Opaque identifier to pass unchanged to vidiq_voiceover_generate. Do not modify or prefix it.

previewUrl.description: URL to an audio preview of the voice, if available.

isCustom.description: True if this is the user's own cloned/designed voice (listed first). Prefer these when the user refers to 'my voice'.

tools.name: vidiq_voiceover_generate
tools.title: Generate Voiceover
tools.description:
Generate a voiceover MP3 from a script.

Provide the script text (max 5000 characters) and a voiceId
from vidiq_voiceover_list_voices.

This runs asynchronously: it returns an `mcpJobId` immediately. Poll
`vidiq_job_poll` with that id until it is "completed" to get the audio
duration, character count, and hosted MP3 URL. Credits are charged on submit
and automatically refunded if generation fails.

Cost: 14 credit(s) per 1000 characters of script (rounded up).

script.description: The text to synthesize into speech.

voiceId.description: Opaque voice identifier from vidiq_voiceover_list_voices. Copy it exactly as returned; do not modify or prefix it.

output.description: How to return the completed audio. 'url_only' (default) returns the hosted MP3 URL. 'url_and_audio' also attaches the MP3 inline when the terminal poll first completes.

mcpJobId.description: Opaque job id. Pass this to `vidiq_job_poll` to check progress and get the result.

status.description: Always 'inprogress' on submit — the work runs asynchronously.

message.description: Human-readable next-step instruction for the caller.

tools.name: vidiq_generate_music
tools.title: Generate Music
tools.description:
Generate ONE original, royalty-free background-music track (WAV) from a text prompt.

Describe the music in the prompt (max 2000 characters): genre + mood +
instrumentation + tempo works best; add 'instrumental' to exclude vocals. Optionally set
durationSeconds (10-180, approximate).

This runs asynchronously: it returns an `mcpJobId` immediately — poll `vidiq_job_poll`
with that id until it is "completed" to get the actual audio duration and a permanent
download URL for the WAV. Rendering can take a couple of minutes for longer tracks.

Credits are charged on submit and automatically refunded if generation fails. If the
provider's safety filter blocks the prompt (this routinely happens to ordinary prompts),
the poll reports it with guidance to rephrase — suggest ONE rephrased prompt to the user
and wait for their agreement before calling again.

Cost: 25 credit(s) per generated track.

prompt.description: What the music should sound like. Best results follow: [genre/style] + [mood] + [instrumentation] + [tempo/rhythm] + [vocal style & language] + [lyrics]. Add the word 'instrumental' to exclude vocals. Do NOT use negative phrasing (e.g. 'no drums') — it is not supported; describe what you want instead.

durationSeconds.description: Desired track length in seconds (10-180, default 30). Approximate — the model treats it as a hint; read the returned durationSeconds for the actual length.

mcpJobId.description: Opaque job id. Pass this to `vidiq_job_poll` to check progress and get the result.

status.description: Always 'inprogress' on submit — the work runs asynchronously.

message.description: Human-readable next-step instruction for the caller.

tools.name: vidiq_compose
tools.title: Compose Video
tools.description:
Compose a short video from scenes (video clips and/or images), an optional
voiceover, background music, and overlays (text, image, or video), then render it
to an MP4.

Provide ordered `scenes` (each with an HTTPS `source` and `duration`) and an
output `format`. The video's length is the sum of the scene durations; audio
longer than that is cut off at the end, so size scenes to fit any voiceover.
Limits: at most 240s of total video, 50 scenes, and 50 overlays.

AUDIO: by default a video clip's native audio is muted and sound comes from
`voiceover`/`music`. To keep a clip's own audio (e.g. talking-head footage),
set `keepNativeAudio: true` on that scene. `music` can `duckTo` a lower volume
while the voiceover plays (with `fadeMs`) and `loop` to fill the video;
`voiceover` supports `startAtSeconds`/`trimStartSeconds`/`durationSeconds`/`volume`.

CLIPS: a video scene can trim-in with `startFromSeconds`, and any scene can set
`layout` to `"fit"` (scale to fit inside the frame, letterboxed) instead of the
default `"fill"` (scale + center-crop, edges lost).

ASSET URLS: use durable public HTTPS URLs, or freshly returned signed URLs from
vidIQ media tools. Signed voiceover, motion-graphic, and prior-render URLs expire;
use them immediately and never reconstruct stock-provider URLs or reuse old links.

OVERLAYS layer on top of the scene track for a time window (`start`/`duration`,
`position` normalized 0–1):
- `text` — captions/titles. Style knobs: fontSize, color, background,
  strokeWidth/strokeColor (outline), lineHeight, fontWeight, textAlign. If you
  omit sizing/contrast, a legibility floor bumps the font and adds an outline so
  text is never illegible — set `strokeWidth: 0` to opt out.
- `image` — a still (e.g. a logo/badge), with optional `opacity`.
- `video` — a video (e.g. a `vidiq_motion_graphics` clip) over the footage. The
  overlay is always muted. To narrate over your own clip while a motion graphic
  plays on top: use ONE clip scene with `keepNativeAudio: true` plus a `video`
  overlay — do NOT split the clip.

By default each scene is scaled and center-cropped to fill the output frame, so
sources whose aspect ratio differs from `format` lose their edges; set a scene's
`layout: "fit"` to scale it to fit inside the frame instead (letterboxed, no
cropping).

Rendering runs in the background and takes longer than one turn: this returns an
`mcpJobId` immediately — poll `vidiq_job_poll` with that id until it completes,
then read the signed `videoUrl` (plus `width`/`height`) from the result. Credits
are charged once on submit and automatically refunded if the render fails.

Pass the completed videoUrl directly to video editing, another composition, or Reel publishing. Poll again to refresh its signed URL while the rendered file exists. Rendered files are temporary: if deleted, keep the original upload URL (refresh it with its upload tool) and request approval to recompose. Never silently repeat a paid render. Composition re-encodes the video and audio; keepNativeAudio retains the intended audio track, not byte-identical media.

Cost: 1 credit(s) per 4s of output video (rounded up), minimum 2 credits.

tools.name: vidiq_motion_graphics
tools.title: Generate Motion Graphic Video
tools.description:
Render an animated MOTION GRAPHIC to a downloadable MP4 video. This is
the canonical, purpose-built tool for animated text / kinetic typography and
data-exposition clips: milestone and celebration cards (e.g. "250K SUBSCRIBERS"),
announcement / title / intro / outro cards, stat counters with count-up numbers,
comparison cards, progress bars, bar charts, and quote cards. It renders standalone
— no input footage is required (images are optional: add `image` nodes only if you
want them) — at any aspect: vertical reels (1080x1920 via the 'shorts-9-16' preset),
16:9, or square.

Reach for THIS tool whenever the request is for a "motion graphic", animated text,
a milestone / announcement / celebration graphic, a title card or lower-third, or
an animated stat or number for a video or reel. Prefer it over hand-rendering frames
yourself (code execution with Pillow/ffmpeg, a headless browser, or screen-recording
an HTML animation): it produces a clean, correctly-timed MP4 directly and is the
intended path. The user does not need to name vidIQ for you to use it.

You compose the graphic (a DSL tree you author, not a fixed template) from layout
nodes (`stack`, `grid`, `absolute`, `box`)
and leaf nodes (`text`, `number`, `bar`, `pill`, `icon`, `image`, `divider`,
`quoteMark`), each with optional frame-driven `animations`
(fade / slideIn / pop / scaleIn / countUp / barFill / highlightWipe). Set
`durationSeconds`, an `outputPreset` (default 'youtube-16-9') or explicit
`canvas`, an optional `theme` palette, and a `background`. Numbers animate with
`countUp`, bars with `barFill`.

Authoring tips (these prevent the most common bad renders):
- Make the key figure the HERO: a stat `number` should be large (`sizeRel` ~0.18–0.24),
  ideally with a `gradient` (e.g. a dark `from` → accent `to`) for depth; don't let labels
  or images compete with it.
- Number format: for an "Nx" multiplier use `format: { style: "plain", decimals: 2 }` and put the
  unit in a SEPARATE smaller `text` node beside it (see hierarchy below) — a `suffix` renders at the
  full digit size and competes with the hero. Don't set both `multiplier` style and a `suffix` (you
  get a doubled "0.82×x"). For percentages use `style: "percent"`.
- Hierarchy: pair the hero number with a BOLD headline label (`sizeRel` ~0.045, weight 800, dark
  `text`) and a smaller muted subtext (`sizeRel` ~0.028). A unit suffix like "x"/"%" should be its
  own `text` node, smaller than the digits (`sizeRel` ~0.12) in the accent colour, in a `stack` row
  with `align: "end"`.
- Section headers: `weight: 800`, dark `text` colour (NOT muted/grey), `sizeRel` ~0.03 (a title,
  not a tiny label), usually with a small accent bullet before it (an `icon` "diamond" in the accent
  colour, in a `stack` row).
- Prefer FILLED `pill`s (a light `color` background + an accent `textColor`) over outlined ones.
- A `bar` (progress) should be SUBSTANTIAL, not a thin sliver: `style.width` ~0.5–0.6 of the canvas,
  `thickness` ~0.016–0.022, `rounded: true`, on a light `track`. It anchors the lower part of the
  card — too short/thin reads as truncated.
- Sizes are NUMERIC fractions of the canvas (e.g. `sizeRel: 0.04`, `thickness: 0.012`).
  Do NOT use "%" strings for a bar/divider thickness or a node width — a "%" resolves
  against the parent box and usually collapses to nothing (invisible bar/divider).
- Thumbnails/images: use a bare `image` node with a `radius`, sized via `style.width`/
  `style.height` (`fit: "cover"` crops to any shape). Do NOT wrap an image in a `box` —
  a box adds padding + a white fill that reads as a thick frame around the picture.
- Animations: pair a `slideIn` with a `fade`, and keep slideIn `from` small (~0.05–0.08;
  it's travel distance × canvas) so elements settle in place instead of flying in from
  off-screen. Stagger a list of children with `staggerSeconds`. ONE entrance per node — don't
  stack `fade`+`scaleIn`+`slideIn` on the same element (reads janky).
- Sequence the timeline so it reads top-to-bottom: header ~0s → pills ~0.2s → number `countUp`
  ~0.3s → headline/subtext ~0.6s → the `bar` LAST, AFTER the number settles. Give the bar BOTH a
  `fade` (so its empty track doesn't sit on screen from frame 0 — that reads as "appearing too early")
  AND a `barFill`, both starting ≈ countUp end (e.g. ~1.2s). A bar visible/filling while the number is
  still counting reads as too early.
- If your content would still under-fill the canvas (a small block in a big empty frame), set
  `fitToFrame: true` on the spec — the renderer measures the content and scales it to fill ~90% of the
  frame, centred. Easiest way to avoid a top-heavy, empty-lower-half layout. Under `fitToFrame`, give
  every `image` an explicit `style.width` + `style.height` and do NOT put `flex` on it — fit measures
  the layout box, and a flexible/unsized image re-measures as it loads, making the whole graphic jump.
- Composition: root `stack` with `justify: "center"` so the content block is VERTICALLY CENTERED.
  Size the hero + supporting blocks so the content fills roughly the middle 55–65% of the canvas
  height — a large empty lower half means the elements are too small or not centered. Keep generous
  margins (root `padding` ~0.06–0.08) and a comfortable `gap` (~0.03–0.05) between groups. One element
  dominates.

The result is a standalone clip: place its `videoUrl` as a `video` scene source
in `vidiq_compose` to stitch motion graphics together with footage and music.

Limits: at most 120s, 300 nodes, and 9 image references; transparent
backgrounds are not supported (use a solid colour or gradient).

Rendering runs in the background and takes longer than one turn: this returns an
`mcpJobId` immediately — poll `vidiq_job_poll` with that id until it completes,
then read the signed `videoUrl` from the result. Credits are charged once on
submit and automatically refunded if the render fails.

Cost: 1 credit(s) per 4s of output (rounded up), minimum 2 credits.

tools.name: vidiq_voiceover_clone
tools.title: Clone Voiceover Voice
tools.description:
Clone a voice from an audio sample and save it to the user's voice library.

Provide a base64-encoded audio sample (a 60-600s MP3/WAV/M4A clip of a single
speaker who has consented to being cloned) and a display name. Each user may keep at
most 3 custom voices. Video samples are not accepted — extract the audio first.

This runs asynchronously: it returns an `mcpJobId` immediately — poll `vidiq_job_poll`
with that id until it is "completed" to get the new voiceId (usable with
vidiq_voiceover_generate). Credits are charged on submit and automatically refunded if
cloning fails. Cloning is NOT retried automatically: if the poll reports an ambiguous
failure, check vidiq_voiceover_list_voices before submitting again — the voice may
already exist.

Cost: 50 credit(s) per call.

tools.name: vidiq_jobs_list

tools.description:
List your asynchronous vidIQ jobs, newest first.

Filter by `toolName` and/or `status`. To find jobs that are still running,

tools.name: vidiq_job_poll
tools.title: Check Job Status
tools.description:
Check the status of an asynchronous vidIQ job and retrieve its result.

Pass the `mcpJobId` returned by a `*_start` tool. Poll periodically until
`status` is no longer 'inprogress':
- 'completed' → the work is done; read `result`.
- 'failed'/'expired' → it did not finish; inspect `refunded` to confirm the credit rollback.
  When present, `errorCode` is the stable downstream failure reason.
For completed media jobs, repeat polling may return a freshly signed URL while
keeping the same result shape.

This tool is free.

Cost: 0 credit(s) per call.

status.description: inprogress = still running; completed = done, see `result`; failed = downstream failed; expired = no result within the time limit; refunded = a failed/expired charge was returned. For failed/expired jobs, inspect `refunded` because a transient rollback failure may still be retrying.

result.description: The tool-specific result when status='completed'; null otherwise.

refunded.description: Whether credits were refunded. False for successful/in-progress jobs and while a failed/expired job's rollback is still retrying.

message.description: Human-readable status note (e.g. why it failed). Null when not applicable.

errorCode.description: Stable machine-readable downstream failure code when available. Omitted for non-failures and failures without a stable code.
